A is also located on the straight lines on which sides AB and AE lie. Reasoning: Apply the generalized Viviani theorem to the regular pentagon: the sum of the perpendicular distances from any point to the straight lines on which the five sides lie is equal to 5 times the inradius. Here the perpendicular distance from O to side CD is OP=1, so the inradius of the pentagon is 1. The distances from point A to the straight lines on which the two sides AB and AE lie are both 0; the distances to the straight lines on which CB, CD, and DE lie are respectively AQ, AP, and AR. Therefore 0+0+AQ+AP+AR=5·1=5. Also, from the figure A, O, P are collinear and O is between A and P, so AP=AO+OP=AO+1. Substituting gives AQ+AR+AO+1=5, therefore AO+AQ+AR=4.

raw_record.question_text: $ABCDE$ is a regular pentagon. $AP$, $AQ$ and $AR$ are the perpendiculars dropped from $A$ onto $CD$, $CB$ extended and $DE$ extended, respectively. Let $O$ be the center of the pentagon. If $OP = 1$, then what is the value of $AO + AQ + AR$?

method.method_draft: Use the generalized Viviani theorem for a regular polygon. Read from the diagram that A lies on the two side-lines AB and AE, so its perpendicular distances to those two sides are 0; the other three side-line distances from A are AQ to line CB, AP to line CD, and AR to line DE. From the text, OP=1 and O is the center, so OP is the apothem/inradius of the regular pentagon. For any point in or on a regular n-gon, the sum of perpendicular distances to all side-lines equals n times the apothem. Hence 0+0+AQ+AP+AR=5·1=5. Since A, O, P are collinear on the symmetry axis and OP=1, AP=AO+OP=AO+1. Therefore AQ+AR+AO+1=5, giving AO+AQ+AR=4.

method.method_draft: Use coordinates/trigonometry. Place O at the origin and put A on the positive y-axis. Since OP=1 is the apothem, the circumradius is AO=R=1/cos36°. The vertices may be taken at central angles A=90°, B=18°, C=-54°, D=-126°, E=162°. The side-line CB has outward unit normal in the direction -18° and is at distance 1 from O. Therefore the perpendicular distance from A=(0,R) to this line is AQ=1+R sin18°. By symmetry, AR=AQ. Thus AO+AQ+AR=R+2(1+R sin18°)=2+R(1+2sin18°). Substitute R=sec36° and use the identity 1+2sin18°=2cos36° to get 2+sec36°·2cos36°=2+2=4.
